STEP 1 - Scene: A bowl of whole raw almonds, a snack portion.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A white paper bowl or plate, about 17 cm across at the rim. The food sits inside a smaller inner area of about 14 cm. Area = 3.14 x 7^2 ≈ 154 cm^2.

STEP 3 - Items: Whole almonds only.

STEP 4 - Area: The almonds cover about 85% of the inner area, which is about 130 cm^2.

STEP 5 - Volume: The pile is heaped about 3 cm high at the center and thinner at the edges, so I use an average of about 2.5 cm. Volume = 130 x 2.5 ≈ 325 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole almonds have a bulk density of about 0.6 g/ml because of the large gaps between them. 325 x 0.6 ≈ 195 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Almonds have about 579 kcal per 100 g. 195 g gives about 1130 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A bowl of this size holds roughly 150-200 g of almonds, which is about 120-170 nuts. I count about 70-90 visible almonds in a single layer, with some stacking. Each almond weighs about 1.2 g, so 100-150 almonds would be 120-180 g. I adjust the total to about 160 g.
